cards.title: Pace of the work: approval gates, or a built draft the owner reacts to
cards.block: Builder > Process > Pace of making (after the system exists; `references/making.md` sections 1, 2 and 9)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) When the person wants to see something built, build the draft on a sketch-level token build and keep three things: every value from the tokens or on the debt list, the page's materials fixed before the second section, and a cohesion check before "done" [inferred]. A stated preference is something to test: build the smallest real version and keep the version before one switch away [inferred]. Heuristic: study shipped examples before inventing options (DC-L19-178); when invented options are rejected, rebuild a few shipped examples on a review page [S-L22-01: D-261012-2926]. "More like this one" asks for new ideas, not near-copies [S-L22-01: D-261011-b965].

cards.title: Comparing options on a built page: switches, a kept baseline, and boiling down
cards.block: Builder > Review > Options on a built page (`references/making.md` section 3; STD-process-review-taste-37 to -49)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) For one piece, the house standards hold as written: three options by default, one at a time, full size, in realistic surrounding context, on a review surface that never ships. Where several questions are open on one page, give each its own switch and keep the current version as an option [inferred from this project's accepted rounds]. Heuristic: count the combinations before adding a switch, because every one must be flipped through before the hand-off (STD-process-review-taste-47); boil down as soon as a question is answered [inferred].

cards.title: What stays the same between sections, and the audit when it did not
cards.block: Patterns > Page composition > Cohesion across sections (`references/making.md` section 4; `assets/output/COHESION-AUDIT.md`)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Vary layout, hold materials [inferred; a companion to DC-L19-50, which asks for varied layouts and limits how far a section may break the grid, and says nothing about type, corners or boxes]. Fix the materials before the second section is built. When the person says the page does not hang together, audit before restyling: the same questions for every section, measured, with each complaint matched to a cause, and at least a least-effort and a most-adaptable direction [inferred from one accepted audit]. A restyle does not change sizes [S-L22-01: E-261012-f5e4; notes]. The counts above are one page's measurements, not limits.

cards.title: Finished interface shown inside a page
cards.block: Imagery > Product views > Live product views inside a page (`references/making.md` section 6)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Whether to show the product rests on DC-L19-131, which says to use the real product; here the views were built for the page with invented data, so this card is about that form only. How: build the view at real size and show it scaled; name the parts that must stay readable and measure them as rendered; keep the two style worlds apart in both directions; after any page-wide restyle, compare the view with the version before; on a phone, crop and move the view instead of shrinking it [inferred from this project's accepted rounds]. Heuristic: if a page rule has no class in its selector, assume it reaches into the embed.

cards.title: Where a built page is checked before it is shown
cards.block: Builder > Verification > Checking the rendered page (`references/making.md` section 5)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) Rests on DC-L19-56, DC-L19-153 and DC-L19-167, which stand. This project adds four habits, each [inferred] from its rework: ask once what the person reviews in and test there; test between the breakpoints; test with no hover; compare with the version before. Heuristic: if the builder has not looked at a screenshot of the change at the person's window size, it has not been checked.

cards.title: Sections that hold the page while they step
cards.block: Patterns > Scroll > Held sections and what moves them on (`references/making.md` section 7)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) DC-L19-84 stands: few moving parts on a site meant to convert, a scroll story only where the page exists to be experienced. This project is one case of a site meant to convert whose owner still wanted two held sections; the cost was measurable, and the owner agreed to shorten both a little once the share was shown. Heuristic: for each held section, report its share of the page's whole scroll, and use one control pattern for all of them [inferred].

cards.title: Figures drawn as graphics on a marketing page
cards.block: Imagery > Data graphics > Proof figures on marketing pages (`references/making.md` section 8)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) The figure alone is a sound start. Add a drawing only when it shows what the words state, in the product's own chart language when the page shows the product [inferred from one accepted and one rejected round]. Heuristic: if the drawing needs an axis the copy does not give, it is claiming something nobody checked.

cards.title: How far a note reaches
cards.block: Builder > Feedback > Scope of a change (`references/making.md` section 2)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) A note changes the thing named and every other instance of the same kind, and nothing of another kind [inferred: the digest counts about 30 decisions that repeat an earlier note, and 15 changes that went too wide]. Say in one line what you will apply it to. Where instances can be counted, count them before and after. Act on what follows from the request and report it; ask only for a real fork, with your pick and a visible alternative; put waiting decisions in one numbered list the person can answer in one message [inferred]. Lane L21 proposes "one example stands for a class" from a different project; this card adds the opposite failure and the count.

cards.title: The builder's recurring mistakes, and what a repeated note means
cards.block: Builder > Feedback > Learning from the person's replies (`references/making.md` section 10)
cards.default: (default + heuristic) A repeated note is a signal about how the builder reads, not only about the thing. On a second mention: stop, re-read both messages, name what was misread (too narrow, too wide, too literal, or the wrong thing), say the rule back in one line, apply it to every instance, and record it so later work keeps it. On a third: write a check that finds every case [inferred from one rule where this was done]. "I like this one, show me more" asks for new ideas at the same level, not variations of it [S-L22-01: D-261011-b965]. Before showing work, check it against the list of mistakes in `making.md` section 10.
